coverage_rules: The panel covers insertion codes, alternate locations, missing residues, nonstandard residues, multichain coordinates, pLDDT, PAE, and experiment-specific wwPDB validation.
Synthetic sequence-mismatch and undeclared-provenance controls are recorded separately from the 16 public cases.

coverage_requirements.rationale: The panel's coverage_rules were prose only. Composition counts records per stratum and split, so a coverage rule could go unmet while the panel reported itself complete -- and insertion codes did exactly that until 1IGT was curated. Each feature is now witnessed from the evidence an executed case produced, and execution fails if any required feature has no witness.

modified_residues.resolution: Either StructQC reports modified residues explicitly, or the panel's coverage_rules drop the claim. For a coordinate-trust tool, a post-translational modification is exactly what a user needs surfaced before mapping a functional residue, so reporting it is the better fix.
modified_residues.status: NOT SATISFIED - recorded as an open defect, not as met coverage
modified_residues.why_not_witnessed: StructQC counts a residue as nonstandard only when its one-letter code is X. A chemically modified residue that maps to its unmodified parent is normalised and never reported. 2V7A chain A contains PTR393 (phosphotyrosine); gemmi sees 271 polymer residues, StructQC reports 270 with nonstandard_residues: 0, and the string PTR appears nowhere in the evidence record, the residue table, or the run manifest.
modified_residues.why_not_worked_around: A detector could read the coordinate file directly, but then the panel would claim coverage of a feature the tool under test does not report. Coverage must be witnessed from the evidence the tool produces, or it is not coverage.

missing_evidence_behavior.detail: Exit 1 is a scientifically-incomplete result carrying its reason, not a failure.
missing_evidence_behavior.rule: The run's missing-evidence list must equal the stratum's declared expectation. Evidence that cannot exist for a stratum is declared, not silently tolerated; anything else appearing there is a change that must be noticed.

nmr.rationale: An NMR entry deposits an ensemble; these range from 10 to 20 models. StructQC evaluates one model, so which one is a scientific choice and is declared per case rather than inherited from a CLI default. Model index 0 (the first deposited model) is used uniformly. Ensemble-wide agreement is a separate question this stratum does not test.

alphafold.note: No wwPDB validation report exists for a predicted model. The official confidence evidence is pLDDT in the B-factor column plus the PAE matrix, so the gate checks those instead of geometry-validation metrics.

cryo_em.note: A cryo-EM validation report carries the same geometry metrics as an x-ray one plus a reported resolution, but no crystallographic R-factors. Resolution is required here because the report supplies it; requiring r_free would fail every case in the stratum.

nmr.note: A solution-NMR validation report carries geometry metrics but neither resolution nor R-factors, because neither exists for the method. The metric set is the geometry core alone.

alternatives.equals_one: Identity must be 1.0 for every case. Disqualifies every structure carrying an engineered mutation, including 2V7A, and with it the panel's only nonstandard-residue coverage.
alternatives.matches_declared_expectation: The computed identity must equal the value declared for the case. A declared engineered mutation is expected to lower identity, and failing to lower it is the defect.

residue_identity.chosen_because: 2V7A measures 0.996296, which is exactly 1 - 1/270: the single declared T315I difference and nothing else. Detecting a declared mutation is the behaviour under test, so the gate asserts the measurement matches what the case declares.
